rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 5 (x ±0.03 m, kp 2.6, kd 0.9, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.2) is the best raced design at 699.16. Oval and s-bend finished 20/20 on both tracks, and the slalom finished 0/20 with max_error 0.0634 and about 1.05 line-loss events. Iteration 8 widened x to ±0.04 m with the same controller. Oval and s-bend stayed at 20/20, but s-bend mean score dropped from 950 to 943 and the total fell to 684.65. The slalom did not change: max_error 0.0635 and 1.0 line-loss events. So wider x coverage has not cleared the slalom limit, and it cost s-bend score. Across iterations 3 to 8, slalom max_error has stayed between 0.0618 and 0.0646 under every kp, kd, ki, x and speed setting tried. The lowest value came from the lowest speed tried so far (1.2 with kp 2.6, kd 0.8: 0.0618). The score is roughly the mean of the three tracks. The slalom contributes about 190 while off track, so a slalom finish is the largest remaining lever.

Change. I return the geometry to the best-scoring layout, x ±0.03 m (-0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03) at y 0.06, and keep the 16 mm footprint, mass 0.6, and wheels unchanged. I also lower base_speed from 1.2 to 1.1, with kp 2.6, kd 0.9, ki 0.05 and sensor_weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] unchanged. This is a single-variable test against iteration 5. Speed is the one lever that has not been isolated: iteration 3 to 4 cut speed and kp together and reduced slalom max_error from 0.0646 to 0.0618, while kd and ki alone did not move it.

Timing check. Oval mean time is 1.83 s at 1.2. Scaling by 1.2/1.1 gives about 2.0 s, and the s-bend gives about 2.43 s from 2.23 s. Both are under the 3.0 s limit with margin, so completion should hold.

Expected result. Oval and s-bend stay at 20/20. Slalom max_error falls to about 0.060 or below, with line-loss events at or below 1.0. A slalom finish is possible but not expected.

Decision rules for the next iteration. If oval or s-bend finish rate falls below 0.95 or completion_time exceeds about 2.8 s, return base_speed to 1.2. If the slalom still ends off track with max_error at or above 0.06 at 1.1 m/s, the controller levers are exhausted, so the next step is to test a different structural change (for example line_loss search_right, or 3 sensors). If any slalom run finishes, hold all values and confirm the score.

Hypotheses. (a) Lower speed reduces slalom overshoot through the sharp alternations. (b) The x ±0.03 layout keeps the s-bend score at about 950, which the wider layout did not. Measurements requested: full set, read per track, with emphasis on slalom max_error, line_loss_events, progress and completion_time, and on oval and s-bend completion_time to confirm the speed margin.
